answer.label: Said and later reaffirmed by
answer.sourceLine: Jiddu Krishnamurti used this formulation in connection with his 1929 dissolution of the Order of the Star. His own 1980 summary, “The Core of the Teachings,” quotes the exact phrase and identifies it as central to his teaching.

source.heading: The source

docMeta.dd: Rejection of prescribed spiritual paths and authority

trail: His 1980 written summary ↗ quotes the exact sentence and explains that truth cannot be reached through an organization, creed or technique.
The Foundation’s booklet description ↗ identifies the earlier address’s date and place; Wikiquote ↗ reproduces the larger speech.

author.name: Jiddu Krishnamurti
author.heading: About Jiddu Krishnamurti
author.bio: Jiddu Krishnamurti rejected the World Teacher role prepared for him by the Theosophical movement and spent decades speaking about freedom from psychological authority and conditioning. His meetings included public talks, audience discussions and dialogues with scientists and teachers; he asked listeners to investigate rather than follow him.

copyAttribution: Jiddu Krishnamurti, 1929 dissolution-address formulation, explicitly reaffirmed in his 1980 “The Core of the Teachings.”

context.heading: Why it mattered
lead: Krishnamurti had been placed at the center of an organization expecting a spiritual teacher. His dissolution address rejects turning that expectation into another religious authority; the later summary makes the same point through personal observation rather than obedience to a prescribed method.
